_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship, give the citation in note), 'provisional' (your romanization, not found in outside sources), 'decided' (a project style call). If you find a better attested form mid-book, change it here AND grep every built chapter for the old form, then rebuild. Sections are rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored. Add/rename sections freely (people, organizations, places, terms, ...).

荣家.note: The Shanghai medicine-trade house at the centre of the novel; Bannermen (旗人).

荣老爷.note: Head of the household; takes four wives in turn.

瑜儿.note: A pet name (瑜) used by Old Madam Rong; apparently Master Rong himself.

大太太.note: The senior wife (大 = senior); runs the household; mother of Rong Sheng.

二太太.note: A rice-merchant's daughter; mother of Rong Gui; dies in the countryside.

三太太.note: A tailor's daughter; mother of the twin daughters.

四太太.note: The bride Jinlian; A-Chu's adoptive mother.

金莲.note: 'Golden Lotus'; the fourth wife. See the note at Chapter 1.

荣归.note: Second son (归, 'return'); born in mourning, raised in the country.

荣初.note: 'Rong the Beginning' (初); the family's youngest son, and the name at the heart of the book's doubling.

阿初.note: The foster boy picked up by Fourth Madam, raised as Rong Sheng's study-companion; becomes a physician. 阿 is a familiar prefix.

荣荣.note: One of the twin daughters of Third Madam.

荣华.note: The other twin daughter of Third Madam.

江丽水.note: A distant niece of First Madam; often 'Lishui.' Comes to Cardiff to find Rong Sheng.

丛惠.note: A wealthy overseas-Chinese merchant's daughter; A-Chu's classmate and love.

丛锋.note: Cong Hui's elder cousin; a radical.

夏跃春.note: A student in the Cardiff circle; later a doctor.

韩禹.note: A student in the Cardiff circle.

霍尔曼.note: Professor Holman, A-Chu's supervisor at the Royal Medical College. English name reconstructed from the transliteration.

玛丽亚.note: A-Chu's neighbour in Cardiff, whose child he delivers.

冬儿.note: A young Rong maidservant, present at the kidnapping.

杨慕次.note: Eldest son of the Yang finance family; a secret Communist agent, codename Drifting Wind.

杨羽柏.note: A magnate of Shanghai finance; Yang Muci's father.

杨家.note: The Shanghai finance house of the Prologue's pear-blossom courtyard.

老余.note: A CCP courier (老 = familiar 'Old'); public identity a financial reporter; codename Timely Rain.

杜旅宁.note: A traveller met on the Hangzhou boat, carrying a crate that is not what it seems.

吴次长.note: A well-connected household the Rongs telephone about the kidnapping.

杜旅宁.note: The boat traveller of Chapter 4; revealed in Chapter 5 as Major-General and Chief of the Juntong Intelligence Section, running the secret Special Police training class.

俞晓江.note: A female major and operative of the Juntong Bureau; Du Luning's aide at the training school and Yang Muci's instructor in ciphers and wireless.

辛丽丽.note: A trainee at the Special Police class, transferred from the Seventh Branch School; first met by Yang Muci at registration.

郭字琼.note: A trainee recruited from the telecommunications school; He Yashan's lover, killed attempting to flee the school.

和雅姗.note: 'He Gege,' of fallen-Qing descent; pregnant and in flight from an arranged marriage, she dies with Guo Ziqiong. See the note at Chapter 6.

和雅淑.note: He Yashan's younger sister; the girl who faints at the Shanghai harbour and is taken to hospital by Rong Sheng.

杏儿.note: Third Madam's clever maidservant; sweet on A-Chu.

阿福.note: The Rong family's driver; a round, portly, devoted man.

二少奶奶.note: Rong Gui's wife, expecting a child in the countryside.

戴局长.note: Dai Li (戴笠), head of the Nationalists' military intelligence. See the note at Chapter 5.

特科.note: The CCP's clandestine intelligence and security service (中央特科), founded 1927 and active in Shanghai; here Yang Muci's and Lao Yu's organ. See the note at Chapter 4.

军统.note: The Kuomintang's Bureau of Investigation and Statistics (secret police). The name is strictly of 1938; its use for 1931 is a mild anachronism. See the note at Chapter 4.

中央警官学校.note: Whose 'Special Police' training class is the cover for Juntong recruitment in the novel.

英国皇家医学院.note: The novel's British medical institution; rendered literally. Britain's actual bodies are the Royal Colleges of Physicians and of Surgeons.

东京大学.note: Where Yang Muci studied; in the 1931 setting its name was Tokyo Imperial University (东京帝国大学).

兰心西餐厅.note: 兰心 ('orchid heart') is the Chinese name of Shanghai's Lyceum.

刘记珠宝行.note: 刘记 = 'Liu's'; the shop from which the Rong child is snatched.

共产党宣言.note: Marx and Engels, 1848. See the note at Chapter 2.

人权宣言.en: the Declaration of the Rights of Man

杭州警察学校.note: The public front through which recruits are funnelled to the Central Police Academy's Special Police class.

虹霞女子学校.note: A Shanghai aristocratic girls' school named in the novel (also 虹霞女子贵族学校, the Hongxia Girls' Aristocratic School).

圣玛利亚女子学校.note: St. Mary's Hall, a real elite girls' school in Republican Shanghai.

明晨女子学校.note: The Shanghai girls' school Xin Lili names as her own.

华美书店.note: The two-story bookstore run by Ronghua.

同济医院.note: Where A-Chu takes a post on returning to Shanghai; 同济 is the real Tongji.

上海白话报.note: A Shanghai newspaper named in the novel.

妇女先锋.note: A women's magazine whose reporters accost Lishui at the harbour.

电讯技术.note: A trade magazine Muci is sent to fetch at the training school.

英国.note: Rendered 'England' or 'Britain' as the sense requires.

卡迪芙.note: In Wales; where Rong Sheng and A-Chu live. See the note at Chapter 3 on the source's 威尔逊卡迪芙.

巴黎.note: Where Cong Hui hopes to open a clinic with A-Chu.

杭州.note: Yang Muci's destination, and the police school's city.

苏区.note: The Chinese Communist base areas of the early 1930s, where Yang Muci wishes to be sent.

梨云阁.note: A courtyard structure in the Rong mansion.

墨菊斋.note: A-Chu's quarters in the Rong mansion.

红梨阁.note: Fourth Madam's quarters in the Rong mansion.

宣统.note: Reign title of the last Qing emperor, Puyi. See the note at the Prologue.

旗人.note: Members of the Manchu Eight Banners. See the note at Chapter 1.

天足.note: Unbound feet, opposed to the bound 'golden lotus.'

黄包车.note: The man-pulled two-wheeled cab of Republican Shanghai.

箫.note: An end-blown vertical bamboo flute of plaintive tone; Rong Sheng's instrument.

飘风.note: Yang Muci's codename. See the note at Chapter 4.

时雨.note: Lao Yu's codename. See the note at Chapter 4.

林潭.note: The recognition passphrase for post-graduation contact.

格格.note: A Manchu title for a daughter of the Qing imperial house or higher nobility. See the note at Chapter 6 (He Gege).
